data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 proposes an inheritance relation: SRC_003 inherits from SRC_005. But SRC_005 is a low-level synchronous program eval that mechanically catches a specific typed lease-mismatch via a code assertion before the provider call, whereas SRC_003 is described as a coverage-decision rubric. A rubric is a decision-making policy, not a program-level type/lease checker; there is no genuine inheritance (method reuse, subtype substitution, or structural refinement) from a single typed code assertion to a coverage rubric. The actual relation is at best a loose 'inspired by' or 'generalises from,' not inheritance. Moreover, the stated refutation condition — that SRC_003's rubric must reject the same homogenization mutation SRC_005 catches — exposes a category mismatch: a rubric's counterconditions (policy-level coverage gates) cannot logically subsume a synchronous-precondition countercondition (a runtime type/lease assertion executed in code). The two operate at different semantic layers (policy vs. runtime check), so the claimed inheritance is refuted by the layer incompatibility itself: you cannot inherit a synchronous program-eval precondition into a rubric and have its counterconditions subsume the program-level ones, because the rubric has no execution-time assertion mechanism. The relation as stated is a mislabelled abstraction, not a genuine inheritance.
